messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with the variance of random effect (inla.expectation)
parts:
On Thu, 2011-04-21 at 08:11 -0700, Martí Casals wrote:
>
> Hi R-inla discussion group,
> My main objective is to guess the variance of random effect
> (nluchador) in my model.I have some problems as you can see below.
> Can someone help me?
>

Hi,

you're almost there...

result$marginals.hyperpar

is a list of marginals. you just have to pick the right one.

the new names for transforming marginals and computing expectations, are
inla.tmarginal() and inla.emarginal().

hopefully this example will clarify the issue.

best,
H


n = 10
y = rnorm(n)
i = 1:n
r = inla(y~1+f(i, model="iid"), data = data.frame(i, y))

print(names(r$marginals.hyperpar))

marg.variance = inla.tmarginal(
function(x) 1/x,
r$marginals.hyperpar$'Precision for i')


plot(inla.spline(marg.variance))
m = inla.emarginal(function(x) x, marg.variance)
mm = inla.emarginal(function(x) x^2, marg.variance)

print(paste("mean", m))
print(paste("sd", sqrt(mm-m^2)))
